topics.title: Overview of Cost Accounting Systems
explain: Business operations require systematic recording of cost and financial transactions.
When cost and financial records are kept separately, it is called a Non-Integrated Accounting System.
When cost and financial records are maintained in a single set of books, it is called an Integrated Accounting System.
Non-integrated systems require periodic reconciliation of profits between cost and financial books.
Integrated systems eliminate the need for reconciliation as there is only one profit figure.

flow.title: Choosing an Accounting System
steps: Record Business Transactions
Select Accounting System Type
If Non-Integrated: Keep Separate Books
If Integrated: Combine in One Book
Reconcile Profits only if Separate

topics.example: A company recording factory costs in a separate costing software and sales in financial accounting software uses a non-integrated system.
remember: Non-Integrated system is also called Cost Control System or Cost Ledger Accounting System.
Reconciliation is NEVER needed in an integrated system.
mistakes: Thinking that integrated accounting requires two separate sets of ledger books.

quiz.q: Under which accounting system is periodic reconciliation of profits required?
quiz.why: Non-integrated system keeps cost and financial records separately, producing two different profit figures that must be reconciled.

quiz.q: What is another name for the Non-Integrated Accounting System?
quiz.why: Non-integrated accounting is also known as Cost Ledger Accounting System or Cost Control System.

topics.title: Non-Integrated Accounting System & Ledgers
explain: Only cost-related transactions like materials, labor, and overheads are recorded in cost books.
Financial items like bank balances, debtors, creditors, and fixed assets are excluded from cost ledgers.
A Cost Ledger Control Account (General Ledger Adjustment Account) is maintained to complete double entry.
Key subsidiary ledgers maintained include Stores Ledger, Work-in-Process Ledger, and Finished Goods Ledger.
Major control accounts include Material Control A/c, Wages Control A/c, Factory Overhead Control A/c, WIP Control A/c, and Cost of Sales A/c.

flow.title: Cost Flow in Non-Integrated Accounting
steps: Purchase Materials to Stores Control A/c
Issue Direct Materials to WIP Control A/c
Add Direct Labour and Factory Overheads
Transfer Completed Output to Finished Goods
Transfer Goods Sold to Cost of Sales
Close Cost of Sales to Costing P&L

topics.example: When raw materials worth ₹5,000 are purchased, cost books debit Stores Ledger Control A/c and credit Cost Ledger Control A/c because cash/creditor accounts do not exist in cost books.
remember: Cost Ledger Control Account represents all financial ledger impersonal accounts.
Materials bought specifically for a special job are debited directly to Work-in-Process Control A/c.
mistakes: Debiting Stores Ledger Control Account for special materials purchased directly for a specific job.

quiz.q: Which account is created in a non-integrated cost ledger to complete double entry for financial transactions?
quiz.why: General Ledger Adjustment Account (or Cost Ledger Control Account) replaces balance sheet accounts in non-integrated cost books.

quiz.q: When materials worth ₹1,500 are purchased specifically for a special job under non-integrated accounts, which account is debited?
quiz.why: Special purchases for a specific job bypass stores and are debited directly to Work-in-Process Control Account.

topics.title: Integrated Accounting System
explain: Integrates cost and financial accounts into a single unified ledger system.
Eliminates the General Ledger Adjustment Account and replaces it with real financial accounts.
Uses actual financial accounts like Bank A/c, Receivables (Debtors) A/c, Payables (Creditors) A/c, and Fixed Assets A/c.
Saves time, reduces accounting effort, and provides a single undisputed profit figure.
Requires pre-requisites like proper cost coding, agreed routines for accruals, and coordinated accounting staff.

flow.title: Transaction Flow in Integrated Books
steps: Transaction Occurs in Factory or Office
Record in Integrated Accounting Ledger
Use Real Accounts like Bank or Creditors
Classify Costs by Job or Process
Generate Combined Financial and Cost Reports

topics.example: When paying wages of ₹1,200 in an integrated system, the entry is Wages Control A/c Dr. to Bank A/c directly.
remember: In integrated accounting, General Ledger Adjustment Account is completely eliminated.
Financial accounts like Debtors, Creditors, and Bank are maintained alongside cost control accounts.
mistakes: Searching for a Cost Ledger Control Account in an integrated ledger trial balance.

quiz.q: Which of the following accounts is eliminated in an Integrated Accounting System?
quiz.why: Integrated system uses real asset/liability accounts like Bank, Debtors, Creditors, so General Ledger Adjustment A/c is eliminated.

quiz.q: What is a key advantage of an Integrated Accounting System?
o: It produces two different profit figures for comparison
It avoids the need for profit reconciliation
It eliminates the need for maintaining subsidiary ledgers
It allows notional costs to be included easily
quiz.why: Since only one set of accounts is maintained, there is only one profit figure, making reconciliation unnecessary.

topics.title: Reconciliation of Cost and Financial Accounts
explain: Necessary when non-integrated books yield different net profits for cost and financial accounts.
Purely financial expenses (e.g., interest on loans, loss on sale of assets, income tax) appear only in financial books.
Purely financial incomes (e.g., dividends received, rent received, interest on deposits) appear only in financial books.
Notional expenses (e.g., notional rent, interest on capital) appear only in cost books.
Differences also arise due to overhead over/under-absorption and varying methods of stock valuation.

flow.title: Reconciliation Procedure Steps
steps: Ascertain Profit as per Cost Accounts
Add Financial Incomes and Over-absorbed Overheads
Add Under-valuation of Opening Stock in Cost Books
Deduct Financial Expenses and Under-absorbed Overheads
Deduct Over-valuation of Closing Stock in Cost Books
Arrive at Profit as per Financial Accounts

topics.example: If dividend of ₹1,00,000 is received, it increases financial profit but is ignored in cost books, so it is added to cost profit during reconciliation.
remember: Under-absorbed overheads reduce costing profit compared to financial profit if financial records record actual expenses.
Notional rent is included only in cost accounts, increasing cost expenses and reducing costing profit.
mistakes: Deducting over-absorbed overheads when starting from Cost Profit to arrive at Financial Profit (over-absorption means cost books took more expense than actual, so costing profit is lower; hence over-absorption must be ADDED back).

quiz.q: Which of the following items is included ONLY in Cost Accounts?
o: Loss on sale of fixed assets
quiz.why: Notional rent is a dummy cost charged in cost books for decision making, whereas financial books record only actual cash expenses.

quiz.q: How is over-absorption of factory overheads treated when reconciling starting from Costing Profit to reach Financial Profit?
quiz.why: Over-absorption means higher overhead was charged in cost books, lowering cost profit. Thus, it must be added back to arrive at financial profit.
